pr_body:
## Breaking Change:

None known

## Description:
Normally, **evohome** reports current temperatures rounded up to the nearest to 0.5 C.

This PR adds the option of high-precision temperatures, to 0.1 C (although they are actually available to 0.01 C):
* add high_precision (current) temperatures 
* bump client to use aiohttp for v1 client
* token saving now event-driven rather than scheduled
* protection against invalid tokens that cause issues
* tweak error message

**Related issue (if applicable):** fixes #27304 via a client bump to 0.3.3b5, see: https://github.com/zxdavb/evohome-async/compare/0.3.3b4...0.3.3b5

**Pull request with documentation for [home-assistant.io](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant.io) (if applicable):** home-assistant/home-assistant.io#<home-assistant.io PR number goes here>

## Example entry for `configuration.yaml` (if applicable):
```yaml
evohome:
  scan_interval: 60
  username: !secret my_evohome_username
  password: !secret my_evohome_password
```

## Checklist:
  - [x] The code change is tested and works locally.
  - [x] Local tests pass with `tox`. **Your PR cannot be merged unless tests pass**
  - [x] There is no commented out code in this PR.
  - [x] I have followed the [development checklist][dev-checklist]

If user exposed functionality or configuration variables are added/changed:
  - [x] Documentation added/updated in [home-assistant.io](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant.io)

If the code communicates with devices, web services, or third-party tools:
  - [x] [_The manifest file_][manifest-docs] has all fields filled out correctly. Update and include derived files by running `python3 -m script.hassfest`.
  - [x] New or updated dependencies have been added to `requirements_all.txt` by running `python3 -m script.gen_requirements_all`.
  - [x] Untested files have been added to `.coveragerc`.

If the code does not interact with devices:
  - [x] Tests have been added to verify that the new code works.

[dev-checklist]: https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/en/development_checklist.html
[manifest-docs]: https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/en/creating_integration_manifest.html

**Home Assistant release with the issue:** 0.99.3
**Last working Home Assistant release (if known):** 0.99.2
**Operating environment (Hass.io/Docker/Windows/etc.):** Ubuntu Server 4.18.0-25-generic

**Integration:** https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/evohome/

**Description of problem:**
Since 2 days the component is not working anymore:

I can however succesful login using the same credentials at the official website at:
https://international.mytotalconnectcomfort.com/Account/Login

comments: Hey there @zxdavb, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with a integration (`evohome`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L92) for? Thanks!

[EDITED by @zxdavb for benefit of future users]

> Am I the only one? did honeywell change things?

No-one else has reported this issue.  I don't think Honeywell is to blame in this instance (although they have been at 'fault' before).

If it was a wrong username/password, the message should be `{"error":"invalid_grant"}` and _not_ `401, message='Unauthorized'`. 

I suspect that HA's storage has been corrupted somehow (more correctly, it contains invalid data for the integration) and your access tokens are invalid (but appear valid).

This is a bit convoluted but what you can do is to create another account on TCC and, using your first account, give the new account permission to access your location.

Then, use those credentials with HA, this should clear the storage - see how that goes.

If that is successful, you will find that switching back to you main account will probably start working (and you can delete the 'new' account).

> Tried using another account (my wife's) and is working fine now:
> Now switched back to my own account, and all is working again... what happened??

This is what I expected (see above).  I will add code to a future release of HA (probably 0.101) to mitigate this issue.

I will close this issue when I submit that PR.
